chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Studio musicians, Lionel Hampton and Chick Webb in the Arnold Shaw book
summary: Hughes cites Arnold Shaw on musicians; Maxine says many studio musicians sat in on 52nd Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. Oh, just let me ask you one more thing. I suppose it was in that Arnold Show
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Yeah, Lionel Hampton and Chick Webb. In those days, I mean, it wasn't unusual for musicians to come and sit in. They had what they called jam sessions. And nine times out of ten the majority of your audience would be made up of musicians anyway. It was, the Onyxs Club was like a lot of the other clubs on 52nd Street, it was easy to get into. The drinks were cheap and the music was good. And the Onyx Club was considered the cradle of swing so it was a very popular place.

A lot of the musicians that worked in the studios and maybe some of the musicians who worked in pit bands would drop in to let their hair heavy down, you know, after they got through playing the arrangements all day.
